title: OpenStax IA 2e Ex. 9.60: tiles/area for x^2 + 6x + 5
stem_student: Use algebra tiles or an area diagram for f(x) = x^2 + 6x + 5. Split the six x-tiles so you can complete a square. Name the side length of that square and the leftover constant before you write any algebra.
stem_teacher: Diagram-only beat on the licensed OpenStax Intermediate Algebra 2e §9.7 Example 9.60 function. Companion algebraic rewrite is mcf3m-m4-openstax-ia2e-ex960-algebraic. Do not reteach transformations (A2.5/A2.6).
answer: Half of 6 is 3, so the completed square is 3 by 3. Leftover constant is 5 − 9 = −4. The picture is (x + 3)^2 − 4.
answer_verification: Copied from OpenStax Intermediate Algebra 2e §9.7 Example 9.60 worked steps (half of 6, square to 9, add and subtract 9; leftover 5 − 9). Student page shows those steps on the algebraic rewrite of the same function.
